issue_context.title: `max` and `min` method of numeric dtypes
issue_context.body:
### Description

It would be great to have something like `i64::MAX` of Rust to quickly call the minimum and maximum literals for each numeric dtype.

For example in Python:

```python
pl.Int8.max # returns `pl.lit(127, pl.Int8)`
```
comments:
same issue, I'm currently using the numpy equivalent as a workaround (but might not always work lol not sure): 

i.e. np.iinfo(np.float32)
We have `upper_bound()` and `lower_bound()` on Series, which does much the same thing - doesn't seem unreasonable to offer it on the dtype (where arguably it's more discoverable/useful) 🤔

review_comments:
I think here we can use something like [`NaiveDate::MAX()`](https://docs.rs/chrono/latest/chrono/naive/struct.NaiveDate.html#associatedconstant.MAX) and `MIN` from chrono here to get date limits, and likewise for `NaiveDateTime`. As an example, the naive date max value is `95026236` and we can see we hit that limit here as well:

```python
import polars as pl

pl.Series([95026236]).cast(pl.Date)  # works
pl.Series([95026237]).cast(pl.Date)  # PanicException: out-of-range date
```

Good point. Perhaps could be discussed in a follow-up issue?

I don't know if we should include chrono limitations here or not.
